_note: Indonesian. Diffed against Malay first, as BACKLOG.md asks, and the answer was
closer than the Turkic four but still not a derivation: 34 of 402 prose cells are
identical at 0.86 mean similarity, and only 3 of the 134 example sentences.
What settles it is not the ratio but the SHAPE of the difference. Taking every
word-level substitution between the two files gives 338 substitutions in 277
distinct types - roughly one type per substitution, a long tail. pt/pt_BR was
derivable because its difference was nine rules applied over and over; this is a
different word in nearly every row. Ten of the pairs recur (adalah/ialah,
tak/tidak, dari/daripada, setelah/selepas, bisa/boleh, film/filem,
kritikus/pengkritik, baru/baharu, tim/pasukan, publik/awam) and they cover well
under a fifth of it.
So: two jobs, written separately. The useful half of the measurement is that the
sentence FRAMES are shared - 0.86 is real - so the Malay row usually differs from
the Indonesian one in its vocabulary rather than its structure. That makes the
second file quicker to write without making it derivable, which is worth saying
plainly because it is the case between the Chinese three and the Turkic four.
The seven specimen quotations stay English. Reported speech was already Indonesian
and stays so. 'Doomscrolling' stays because it IS the specimen of a new coinage,
and 'who' / 'whom' stays because it is an English distinction Indonesian lacks.
english_ok is mathesis alone. Elsewhere the plainer Indonesian word was reached
for: soporific to mengantukkan, plumb-line to unting-unting, seneschal to kepala
rumah tangga, anchorite to pertapa, canaille to gerombolan hina.
dint kept the English preposition 'by dint of' bodily inside the sentence, which is
the same fault kk and ky had; it is 'berkat latihan keras' now.
